action.short_description: H.R.1 House reconciliation package: selected border, detention and asylum-fee provisions
action.compact_description: The H.R.1 House package would fund border infrastructure and adult/family detention capacity and require asylum filing and yearly pending-application fees, initially at least $1,000 and $100 respectively. The passage vote covers the whole package, with its qualifications.
action.meaning: This May22 House passage is the whole H.R.1 reconciliation package, not a separate immigration-only vote. The controlling House choice uses H.Res.436: Rules Committee Print119-3 modified by the amendment printed in H.Rept.119-113 was considered adopted. The retained Immigration clauses are reconstructed against that chain and the contemporaneous as-amended floor Record. The currently served EH incorporates later corrections and renumbering and is a comparison witness for these unchanged selected clauses, not the controlling entire vote-time text. Later engrossment corrections and the July Senate replacement are not silently substituted for this choice. The description selects border infrastructure, detention, State reimbursement and asylum-fee mechanisms; it does not inventory every immigration-related tax, benefit, employment-authorization, child-sponsor or removal provision in this multi-domain package. Section60001 would make additional fiscal2025 CBP appropriations available until September30,2029: $46.5billion for primary/waterborne/secondary barriers, access roads and associated detection attributes; a separate $50million for specified invasive plants impeding RioGrande border operations; and $5billion for CBP facilities/checkpoints near the southwest, northern and maritime borders. These are different purposes, not one immigration-enforcement account or actual expenditures. The adopted manager amendment adds section60004: $12billion in additional fiscal2025 DHS funds, available until September30,2029, for grants reimbursing States for costs of actions on or after January21,2021 assisting federal border/immigration enforcement, including detention/removal and combating unlawful entry of persons/contraband. Applications need satisfactory cost evidence, and DHS cannot reimburse a State already reimbursed under another DHS grant program. This is funding subject to a process and conditions, not proof of State awards or a newly conferred State removal power. Section70101 would appropriate an additional $45billion for fiscal2025 to ICE, available until September30,2029, solely for single-adult alien detention and family residential-center capacity. DHS MAY detain family units pending a removal decision and, if ordered removed, until removal. Its family-center definition includes accompanied alien children, excludes unaccompanied alien children, and expressly applies regardless of State/local facility licensing. Its single-adult detention standards clause says they shall be set in the Secretary's SOLE discretion. Preserve that printed language without importing the Senate's express consistent-with-applicable-law qualification or deciding its interaction with judicial/other legal constraints. The existing unaccompanied-child definition in6USC279(g)(2) requires no lawful immigration status, age under18, and no US parent/legal guardian or none available for care/physical custody; childhood alone does not establish that category. Capacity funding and permission are not a universal detention mandate, removal order or actual detention outcome. Section70002 would require an additional fee at the time an alien files an asylum application: the fiscal2025 amount may be set by rule but cannot be less than $1,000. It cannot be waived/reduced. From fiscal2026 its amount increases using the prior fiscal-year fee and the printed July-to-July CPI-U increase, with the increment rounded down to a multiple of $10. Half of the Attorney-General-filed receipts go to EOIR; half of DHS-filed receipts go to USCIS's existing Immigration Examinations Fee Account; those credited amounts may be retained/spent without further appropriation, and the remainder goes to Treasury. Section70010 separately requires a fee for EACH CALENDAR YEAR an application remains pending, initially at least $100 for fiscal2025, with later CPI-U adjustment, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction. Its printed adjustment has no express rounding term; the filing-fee rounding rule is not copied into it. These are separate filing and pending-application charges, not fixed lifetime amounts or a claim that every asylum applicant actually paid. Section70023 changes existing INA208(d)(3)/8USC1158(d)(3) from MAY impose fees to SHALL, strikes the following cost-cap/installment/nonmandatory-fee language and preserves authority to set additional adjudication/naturalization fees under286(m). The existing paragraph already allowed fees for asylum consideration, employment authorization and asylum-based adjustment and capped them at adjudication costs; the bill does not create first-ever fee authority or establish a new substantive asylum eligibility test through that edit. Existing1356(m)/(n) supply the account/cost-recovery context. Other package provisions and qualifications remain outside these selected highlights. Support/opposition applies only to passage of the entire House proposal; neither component preferences, enactment, legal enforceability nor policy outcomes follow from the vote.
limitations: Selected source-bound Immigration highlights, not an exhaustive package or immigration-component inventory. The whole reconciliation measure also addresses taxes, benefits, defense, education, energy and other policies; a package vote cannot establish a separate position on any highlighted or omitted component.

House70101 prints a State-licensing-independent family-center definition and SOLE discretion over single-adult standards. It cannot be replaced by Senate90003's differently qualified text. Detention-law/judicial interactions require separate review; no universal custody duty, individual removal or legal enforceability ruling is inferred.

All listed appropriations are additional fiscal2025 amounts with September30,2029 availability. The State reimbursement provision requires qualifying post-January21,2021 costs and satisfactory evidence and bars specified duplicate DHS reimbursement. Availability is not actual spending, awards, detention or removal.

Asylum filing and yearly pending-application fees are separate additional charges with fiscal2025 floors, not guaranteed exact prices; the recurring trigger is each calendar year pending. Filing-fee CPI increments round down to $10; the House yearly-fee formula prints no rounding rule. Both have express no-waiver/reduction clauses.

The pre-vote INA fee paragraph already authorizes fees. Its MAY-to-SHALL edit and deletion of cost-cap/installment/nonmandatory language are distinguished from initial authority and substantive asylum eligibility. No later fee implementation rule or PublicLaw119-21 is imported as the pre-vote baseline.

H.Res.436/RCP119-3/adopted119-113 amendment control the May22 choice. June11H.Res.499/492 corrections and the July1EAS are separately recorded version events, not back-projected; the capturedEH is later corrected/renumbered and only the independently compared retained clauses are used here. The later Senate concurrence remains another question in this same episode without a trajectory claim.

choice_meanings.Yea: supported passage of the complete H.R.1 House reconciliation proposal, with the described selected Immigration provisions
choice_meanings.Nay: opposed passage of that complete House proposal; no preferred alternative or separate component position is established
